title: Target-layer commitment experiment
scope: Synthetic target decisions before motion feasibility; no plant, robot, executed command, jerk, contact, or VLA performance claim.
units: SI: position in metres, time in seconds. SVG uses millimetres for readability.

definitions.noise: Exactly +epsilon at even sample indices and -epsilon at odd indices.
definitions.dwell: Accept latest proposal when at least 100 ms passed since the last dwell acceptance; first proposal accepted at t=0.
definitions.lowpass: y[k]=y[k-1]+(1-exp(-dt/tau))*(proposal[k]-y[k-1]); initial y[-1]=0. Standard sampled one-pole recursion.
definitions.gate: Accept proposal iff abs(proposal-anchor)>H; otherwise retain anchor. This does not run motion-feasibility checks.
definitions.variation: Sum of absolute changes in selected targets, including change from initial target 0 to the first selected target.
definitions.onset: First post-event selected target >=0.75 mm above initial 0; delay from event. A target-decision threshold, not physical onset.
definitions.acquisition: First sample at or after onset and after the final intended target becomes constant, such that every remaining selected target is within 0.75 mm of that final truth. Delay is reported from the event and from establishment of the final target. Finite sampled test only.
definitions.hold_windows: Closed time windows listed in each method's metrics. Truth is constant on each window; max and RMS errors are sampled.
definitions.sample_phase: Main plot is 50 Hz. Separate exact replays at 100 and 200 Hz expose parity sensitivity: dwell spans 5, 10, and 20 samples respectively. Even parity aliases the alternating noise to a constant. Noise frequency also changes with cadence, so this is not a same-continuous-disturbance experiment or universal performance ranking.

truth_definitions.slow_drift_3mm: 0 m until 0.5 s; linear 0.0015 m/s ramp to 0.003 m at 2.5 s; hold thereafter.

fixed_hold.title: Fixed hold: noise can be ignored

step_20mm.title: 20 mm step: large changes pass the gate

slow_drift_3mm.title: 3 mm slow drift: commitment creates lag

small_move_1mm.title: 1 mm intentional move: the gate misses it

tradeoffs: Raw targets track bounded-noise truth closely but change at every proposal.
Minimum dwell reduces update count; it does not eliminate target jumps or guarantee smooth physical motion.
Low-pass filtering reduces alternating noise but delays transitions and retains residual oscillation.
The strict gate rejects all fixed-hold noise here and accepts the large step; it delays slow drift and ignores the intentional 1 mm move.
Gate count and variation bounds use variation of true targets at acceptance times; they do not bound robot path length.
verification: Exact Fraction assertions passed for all gate conditions, error bounds, accepted-history variation and count inequalities. Filter metrics and SVG are floating-point numerical output.
